requirement:
The `{term}` role followed by a backtick-delimited full definition name MUST reference a named definition. In rendered Markdown, the reference MUST display the definition's phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to its anchored declaration, without a badge. The phrase MUST be escaped appropriately for rendering.

Missing targets and targets of another kind MUST be reported. Escaped references and references in Markdown code examples MUST remain literal. A term reference MUST NOT satisfy a requirement citation or a Rust function's requirement-coverage obligation.
rationale: I found no gap against `requirements.definitions.references`. Each obligation maps to an `{impl}` item and has a test carrying a `{test}` reference to the subject. **Rendering a `{term}` reference as a plain link** - `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` calls `replace_references`, which calls `replace_inline_references`. - For a `Term` reference whose target is a term definition, `replace_inline_references` emits `phrase`. It uses no badge. - The phrase goes through `terms::escaped_phrase`, and the href goes through `escape_html`. - `tests/definitions.rs#fn[phrases_are_plain_links_and_markdown_literals_are_preserved]` asserts all of this: - the anchored declaration id exists; - there is no `shields.io` badge; - the href points to `../glossary.html#habeas-definition-glossary.a`; - the phrase is escaped to `*alpha* & <beta>`. **Escaped references and Markdown code examples stay literal** - `reference_roles` skips matches that are escaped or inside protected ranges. Protected ranges are code spans and fences. - The same test has an inline-code, a fenced-code and a backslash-escaped reference. It asserts exactly one rendered href, so none of the literals was rewritten. - `definition_schema_deletion_and_literal_references_are_checked` shows that literal and escaped references produce no validation errors and need no definition inputs. **Missing targets and targets of another kind are reported** - In `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_references]`, a `Term` reference whose target is missing or is not a term definition produces "term … has no matching named definition". - `{impl}`, `{cite}` and `{test}` references to a term definition produce "has no matching requirement or example". - `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` covers missing targets and a requirement used as a term target. - `references_to_a_definition_of_another_kind_are_reported` covers an example used as a term target. It also covers `{impl}`, `{cite}` and `{test}` pointing at a term. **A term reference never satisfies a citation or function coverage** - `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[unreferenced_items]` has a `counts` closure that returns false for `Term` references, so a term reference never covers a Rust function. - `references_to_a_definition_of_another_kind_are_reported` asserts that `fn uses` is still reported as uncovered. - `outline_inputs_capture_terms_without_counting_them_as_citations` asserts that a function with only a `{term}` comment is still uncovered. - For requirement citations, `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[examples_may_reference_their_requirement_with_cite_or_test]` asserts that an example whose only reference is a `{term}` naming the requirement still gets the "must reference at least one requirement" error. I found no unspecified behavior in the `{impl}` code, and no reachable obligation lacks a test.
